# Cadre 4.0.0

Cadre 4.0.0 consolidates delivery onto one receipt-based mutation contract,
removes retired runtime APIs and ships only immutable template set v6. Codex,
Claude Code and the native Zed Agent remain stable integrations.

## Changes

- Fix active revisions that could leave canonical state and Autonomous scope
  authority on different revisions. Preserve completed work, original authority,
  review history and resumable recovery.
- Harden review retry, completion, archive, refresh and revert against stale
  proposals, repeated commits, interrupted promotion and changed evidence.
- Retain all ten workflows, four approval modes, sequential/parallel scheduling,
  retained context and historical evidence.
- Remove `archive_batch_record`, `setup_record_commit` and
  `setup_record_git_initialized`. Direct MCP integrations must use operation
  receipts and `candidate_apply` reconciliation; 22 MCP tools remain.
- Ship v6 templates only. Compatible schema-2/v5 projects created with 3.9.x
  continue without migration or metadata rewriting.
- Reconcile public documentation, improve metadata and internal-link validation,
  fix excessive blank space above the mobile homepage, and add visible npm links.

This release includes the fixes recorded in the unreleased 3.9.2 development
notes. The previous published release was 3.9.1.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npm install -g cadre-ai@4.0.0
cadre-ai --version
cadre-ai doctor
cadre-ai install --target all --scope user
```

Reload your client. Compatible 3.9.0/3.9.1 schema-2/v5 projects do not require a
refresh. Unsupported older formats receive `PROJECT_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: install
3.9.0 first, reconcile pending operations and perform its approved refresh
migration, then install 4.0.0. Existing inconsistent operations still require
approved recovery; installation does not rewrite approval records.

## Verification

All 480 harness tests passed, along with types, package validation, pack dry run
and the complete docs check. Native installation and server activation passed on
Codex, Claude Code and Zed. Fourteen native Codex sessions exercised a disposable
brownfield lifecycle including interruption, revision, review/remediation,
manual-edit rejection, archive recovery and refresh. This representative run used
Autonomous approval and sequential scheduling; it is not exhaustive native-mode
coverage. Website checks passed at desktop, mobile and tall mobile sizes with
JavaScript both enabled and disabled.

## Upcoming, opt-in capabilities

- Deeper GitHub/GitLab integration for coordination across multiple people.
- A knowledge base built during delivery and reused as context.
- Polyrepo coordination with per-repository history and approvals.

All three are planned, independently opt-in and disabled by default; they are
not shipped in 4.0.0.

See [documentation](https://cadre-docs.pages.dev/),
[npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cadre-ai),
[validation](https://github.com/vishal-kr-barnwal/cadre/blob/release-4.0.0/docs/development/cadre-4.0.0-release.md)
and [full changes](https://github.com/vishal-kr-barnwal/cadre/compare/release-3.9.1...release-4.0.0).
